## R Chunks

``` {r setup, include=FALSE}
library(ggplot2)
options(digits = 2)
```

``` {r analysis, label="r-chunk-1", echo=TRUE}
data <- data.frame(x = 1:10, y = rnorm(10))
summary(data)
```

``` {r plotting, label="fig-scatter", fig-cap="A scatter plot", fig-width=6}
plot(data$x, data$y)
```

## Python Chunks

``` {python, warning=FALSE}
import pandas as pd
df = pd.DataFrame({'x': range(10)})
print(df.head())
```

``` {python, label="python-analysis"}
import numpy as np
result = np.mean([1, 2, 3, 4, 5])
```

``` {python, label="fig-hist", fig-cap="A histogram"}
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
plt.hist([1, 2, 2, 3, 3, 3, 4])
plt.show()
```

## Julia Chunk

``` {julia}
using Statistics
data = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]
mean(data)
```

## SQL Chunk

``` {sql, #| connection: con}
SELECT * FROM users WHERE active = true
```

## Bash Chunk

``` {bash}
echo "Hello from bash"
ls -la
```

## Mermaid Chunk

``` {mermaid}
graph LR
    A --> B
    B --> C
    C --> A
```

## OJS Chunk

``` {ojs}
viewof x = Inputs.slider([0, 100])
```

## Unknown Language

``` {stata}
summarize mpg
```

## Inline Code

We use inline R code like `r nrow(df)` and Python code like `{python} len(x)`.
